articles.title: Cheniere to fuel QatarEnergy with US Gulf Coast LNG through 2054
articles.summary: The multi-decade deal enables Cheniere to supply QatarEnergy with 4 million tonnes a year from its Gulf Coast facilities, starting in the early 2030s.
articles.body: Business & Finance October 23, 2026 · 9 hours ago Cheniere to fuel QatarEnergy with US Gulf Coast LNG through 2054 The multi-decade deal enables Cheniere to supply QatarEnergy with 4 million tonnes a year from its Gulf Coast facilities, starting in the early 2030s. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Corpus Christi LNG terminal operated by Cheniere Energy on the La Quinta Ship Channel in Corpus Christi, Texas, USA. Source: Bechtel In a move that reflects long-term energy planning, the U.S. Gulf Coast is locking in its commercial ties for the next three decades, as U.S.-headquartered energy player Cheniere has shown with a landmark liquefied natural gas (LNG) deal with Qatar’s state-owned oil and gas giant QatarEnergy, signing on to deliver millions of tonnes of LNG straight through 2054. Cheniere Energy’s subsidiaries, Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL) and Corpus Christi Liquefaction (CCL) , have each entered into long-term LNG sale and purchase agreements (SPAs) with QatarEnergy to supply a total of 4 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG through 2054. Jack Fusco , Cheniere’s Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented: “These pivotal, multi-decade agreements with QatarEnergy, one of the world’s most important energy companies and a cornerstone of the global LNG industry, represent a major long-term commercial commitment and reinforce Cheniere’s position as the leader in U.S. LNG. “We take pride that Cheniere’s track record of operational excellence, reliability and long-term customer focus provided the foundation for this landmark commercial relationship with QatarEnergy. We look forward to reliably supplying QatarEnergy from both Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi into the second half of this century.” While confirming the two SPAs for the purchase of LNG from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi facilities in Louisiana and Texas respectively, located along the United States Gulf Coast, QatarEnergy explained that these deals reflect its continued confidence in the long-term role of LNG in the global energy mix and its efforts to further develop a flexible, diversified, and globally competitive LNG portfolio. The SPAs were signed by Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi , Qatar’s Minister of State for Energy Affairs, President and CEO of QatarEnergy, and Jack Fusco , Chairman, President and CEO of Cheniere Energy. Minister Al-Kaabi said: “The signing of these two SPAs marks an important milestone in our LNG strategy. This major long-term purchase will expand and diversify our global LNG portfolio and advance our ability to meet the evolving requirements of the market. “The additional volumes will complement QatarEnergy’s existing LNG supplies, enhance our supply and trading portfolio, and strengthen our ability to serve customers across the globe.” The Qatari giant has agreed to purchase 2 mtpa of LNG from each of SPL and CCL on a free-on-board (FOB) basis for a purchase price indexed to the Henry Hub price plus a fixed fee. The deliveries under the SPAs will begin in the early 2030s and continue through the end of 2054, with 1 mtpa of the SPL SPA subject to a positive final investment decision (FID) for the first phase of the SPL Expansion project. Related Articles Clean Fuel Bechtel in charge of EPC scope for Cheniere’s LNG terminal expansion project 3 min read Cheniere Energy Partners is developing an expansion of the existing Sabine Pass liquefaction project with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities, which would grow the total production capacity of the SPL project to over 50 mtpa of LNG. The U.S. player expects to execute the SPL Expansion project in a phased approach, with the first phase anticipated to include a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal. This phase has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. In May 2026, the lump sum, turnkey engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract was penned with Bechtel Energy for the first phase of the SPL Expansion project, and the firm was given the go-ahead for early engineering and procurement under a limited notice to proceed (LNTP). Cheniere’s liquefaction portfolio consists of the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast, with total production capacity of approximately 56 mtpa of LNG in operation and an additional approximately 5 mtpa of expected production capacity under construction, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. articles.title: Taylor Maritime agrees final owned bulker sale ahead of London exit
articles.summary: London-listed Taylor Maritime has agreed to sell its last owned bulk carrier for $15.1m, taking its fleet disposal programme to 56 vessels and putting total proceeds on course to reach almost $933m. The Ed Buttery-led company said the final sale is expected to complete in December, bringing to an end a three-year...
articles.body: Dry Cargo Europe Greater China Taylor Maritime agrees final owned bulker sale ahead of London exit Adis Ajdin October 23, 2026 0 153 1 minute read London-listed Taylor Maritime has agreed to sell its last owned bulk carrier for $15.1m, taking its fleet disposal programme to 56 vessels and putting total proceeds on course to reach almost $933m. The Ed Buttery-led company said the final sale is expected to complete in December, bringing to an end a three-year selling campaign that has steadily dismantled one of the largest geared dry bulk fleets in the market. Since the beginning of 2023, Taylor Maritime has executed 55 vessel disposals with expected gross proceeds of $917.7m, at an average discount of 3.5% to fair market value. The latest agreement will lift the total to approximately $932.8m once completed. The move follows the completion of three handysize disposals announced earlier this month, which generated $48.6m. Those deals included transactions involving Buttery’s privately controlled T3 Holding vehicle, which acquired one vessel outright and a majority stake in a company holding another two handysizes alongside Hermes World Maritime. While the latest agreement covers Taylor Maritime’s last owned ship, one vessel remains on charter under a sale-and-leaseback arrangement with a purchase option. That contract expires in April 2027, and the company is assessing the most efficient way to exit the arrangement. Taylor Maritime expects to cease all commercial shipping operations by the end of 2026, with the wind-down now moving towards its final shareholder distributions. The company has confirmed a fourth compulsory capital return of $45m in November, taking the amount returned to investors since January to $263.4m. A further redemption is expected to be announced in December, subject to completion of the remaining vessel sale. The board then intends to put forward plans to cancel the company’s London listing. Taylor Maritime, which floated in May 2021, built its fleet to more than 50 vessels following the takeover of Grindrod Shipping before reversing course and embarking on an extensive asset disposal programme. The company formally adopted a managed realisation strategy in March this year, prioritising vessel sales and the return of capital to shareholders over continued fleet operations. articles.body: Americas Asia Shipyards HD Hyundai and Kiewit to build new US shipyard Sam Chambers October 23, 2026 0 182 1 minute read South Korea’s HD Hyundai has agreed to establish a joint venture with US engineering and construction giant Kiewit to build a new American shipyard, targeting operations from 2029. The venture, HD Kiewit Shipbuilding, plans to begin construction in 2027 at a yet-to-be-announced US industrial site. HD Hyundai expects the facility to create around 3,000 jobs once fully operational. The partners signed the agreement in Houston on Thursday, expanding a strategic shipbuilding partnership announced in July. The greenfield yard will incorporate HD Hyundai’s Future of Shipyard production model, including digital twins, automated manufacturing and robotic welding. It will target US Navy auxiliary vessels and commercial shipbuilding contracts, while also exploring the production of ship blocks and modules for other American yards. The move deepens HD Hyundai’s involvement in Washington’s efforts to revive domestic shipbuilding, supported by South Korea’s $150bn maritime investment commitment. The Korean group has been steadily expanding its American partnerships. In July, it signed an agreement with Fraser Industries to modernise Great Lakes shipyards, while August saw the launch of an automated welding pilot with Huntington Ingalls Industries at its Ingalls Shipbuilding facility in Mississippi. HD Hyundai has also partnered with Edison Chouest Offshore’s Tampa Ship to develop US-built LNG dual-fuel containerships, providing design, procurement and construction expertise. Its robotics division secured orders earlier this year to supply automated welding systems to Chouest yards in North America and Brazil. Unlike compatriot Hanwha’s acquisition of Philly Shipyard, HD Hyundai is pursuing newbuild yard development alongside upgrades to existing American facilities. articles.title: New index tracks how much the world cares about shipping
articles.summary: A new online index – much trailed on Splash – measuring how much attention the global shipping industry receives has gone live, offering maritime companies a way to assess public interest in shipping news and major incidents. Created by crisis communications specialist Dustin Eno, the Maritime Attention Index...
articles.body: Operations New index tracks how much the world cares about shipping Sam Chambers October 23, 2026 1 450 1 minute read Maxar Technologies Maxar Technologies A new online index – much trailed on Splash – measuring how much attention the global shipping industry receives has gone live, offering maritime companies a way to assess public interest in shipping news and major incidents. Created by crisis communications specialist Dustin Eno, the Maritime Attention Index combines Google searches, Wikipedia page views, social media activity and mainstream news coverage into a single daily score. “I built the index to answer a simple question with a single number: how much attention is shipping getting right now?” Eno explained. “Media monitoring tells you how much is being published about shipping, not how much attention it gets.” The publicly accessible platform allows users to examine historical attention spikes, compare incidents and identify how quickly public interest fades. Disasters such as the Ever Given, Wakashio and Dali casualties all show spikes. Eno’s analysis also reveals remarkably consistent patterns in how interest fades after major maritime incidents. When adjusted for duration and intensity, the attention curve surrounding this year’s Iran conflict closely resembles those generated by the Ever Given grounding and Baltimore bridge collapse. The index, which Eno has previously used in Splash commentary, is now available as an interactive public resource, accompanied by monthly analysis. Today’s reading stands at 69.3, with a score of 50 deemed normal. By way of comparison, in the opening fortnight of the US attacks on Iran in March this year, the index shot up to 332.3 points. The index goes back to the start of the 2020s, with its all-time high being the Ever Given’s closure of the Suez Canal in 2021. Christened Focus Stage, the fresh platform will be situated in Hall G, a striking new glass area forming the main entrance to the exhibition halls. Its 2027 debut will be marked by dedicated day-long programmes on Maritime AI, Ports, and maritime marketing and communication. All programmes are developed by leading experts in the three areas. Time to Focus “Nor-Shipping, like the industry we serve, constantly evolves,” comments Sidsel Norvik, Nor-Shipping Director. “Our international audience come here not just to make connections and do business, but also to understand the very latest industry developments, helping them identify opportunity and make informed, profitable decisions. “Focus Stage gives us a new way to meet that demand and deliver value. By joining with expert partners and dedicating an entire day to just one topic, we can explore it from different perspectives, bring relevant expertise together and give visitors a deeper understanding of what comes NEXT.” The new platform complements the established Blue Talks as part of Nor-Shipping’s open-session offering. Its daily focus allows programmes to develop around specific audiences, while topics can change between editions to reflect emerging priorities and opportunities. Designed to deliver Focus Stage announces its arrival on Tuesday 8 June with a day-long dive into one of the topics shaping shipping discussions across the globe: Maritime AI. The sessions, in collaboration with The Norwegian Maritime AI Centre, will shine a spotlight on innovations, collaborations and the practical applications of AI across the industry value chain, helping the audience navigate risk and embrace opportunity. Wednesday 9 June shifts the focus to Ports, exploring the latest steps in smart port development, digitalisation, sustainability, infrastructure, and collaborative approaches. It’s a unique chance to discover how ports are adapting to new technologies, evolving logistics demands, and the transition towards more efficient, connected, and resilient port ecosystems. The Norwegian Ports Association is a partner for the day’s programme. The final day of the 2027 Focus Stage turns the spotlight on Marketing and Communications, a professional community that rarely has its own dedicated arena at major maritime events. Two special awards will be included in the day’s activities, the Stand of the Year and the Voice of the Year. Broadening horizons Speaking of the 10 June topic, Norvik explains: “Effective marketing and communications help maritime companies build visibility, strengthen relationships and communicate value in an increasingly competitive and complex industry, which is what exhibiting at Nor-Shipping is all about! These professionals work extremely hard and we see this as an opportunity to give them a dedicated platform, while also recognising their efforts with the new awards. This adds another dimension to the Nor-Shipping experience. “More broadly, that’s what Focus Stage is about: creating a platform for deeper exploration of relevant topics, while making insights and expertise accessible to all Nor-Shipping visitors. We want people to find content that speaks directly to their work, but also discover perspectives and connections they might otherwise miss.” All Focus Stage programmes feature open sessions, allowing visitors to drop in, leave for meetings and exhibition visits, and return when desired. Alongside the new stage, the Nor-Shipping 2027 programme will feature the Ocean Leadership Conference, Blue Talks, a range of industry conferences, Technical Seminars, regional spotlights, Ocean Campus and AfterWork@AkerBrygge, bringing the global industry together in Norway for business, knowledge sharing and networking.
